## Maturity ladder

| Rung | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `stub` | Named and placed on the spine. Its purpose is not yet stated. |
| `outlined` | Purpose, scope and the main relations are stated. A reader can tell what it is for and where it sits. |
| `specified` | Complete enough to build from: every field, section and relation required for its type and tier is present, applicable probes are dispositioned and nothing blocking is open. |
| `verifiable` | Specified, and every requirement, rule and flow has a defined way to prove it: acceptance tests, or an explicit non-test method. |

## Tiers

| Tier | Name | Review every | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Critical | 60 days | Money moves, access is granted, data can be lost or exposed, a legal duty applies, or the core promise of the product depends on it. |
| 2 | Important | 120 days | A common workflow, or a visible part of the core experience. |
| 3 | Supporting | 240 days | Low risk, easy to reverse, or cosmetic. |

## Statuses that are not maturity

| Dimension | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approval | `draft`, `proposed`, `approved` | Authority. Bound to a hash of the content; only named human approvers. |
| Lifecycle | `active`, `deprecated`, `retired` | Place in the product's life. Retired elements are kept and excluded from coverage. |
| Origin | `human`, `agent`, `skeleton`, `import` | Where it came from. Skeleton elements are prompts nobody has confirmed. |

## Adoption levels

| Level | Types | Adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | 17 | The smallest set that still gives a traceable product definition: intent, actors and permissions, structure, flows, requirements, rules, entities, tests, and the decision, assumption and question registers. |
| `standard` | 21 | Adds research and segmentation, personas, surfaces and screens, use cases and journeys, messages, state machines, events, APIs and integrations, plans and entitlements, obligations, risks, metrics, evidence and releases. |
| `full` | 4 | Adds competing alternatives, principles, system-component references and runbooks. |

## The spine

| Zoom | Type | Question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `PROD` Product | What is this product, and why does it exist? |
| 1 | `DOM` Domain | Which bounded areas make it up? |
| 2 | `CAP` Capability | What can the product do in each area? |
| 3 | `FEAT` Feature | Which deliverable behaviours realise each capability? |
| 4 | satellites | Everything anchored on a feature: flows, screens, rules, requirements, tests. |
